features.title: Hydrate a per-record domain one record at a time
features.summary: Owned fork of the native storage domain form: a per-record domain whose records are disposable derived data indexes document keys at open and reads one record per table read behind a 64-row LRU, instead of materializing the whole unit into JS heap at open. The measured owner is session_projcache, whose ~2.8k checkpoints cost 252 MB of a 610 MB Host heap before this fork. Reads stay synchronous and schema-validated, writes stay durable before memory changes, and every domain that does not qualify (single layout, or per-record over authoritative records) keeps the upstream open-time loadAll. It also adds `KvTable.putMany`: a multi-record write that is ONE durable publish when the backend publishes the unit as one document (a `single`-layout unit's `putRecords`), instead of one full-document rewrite per record.
failureModes: keys() and size count stored documents, so a document that parses as foreign stays counted until its first read drops it from the index.
A schema failure on a disposable record is backed up and skipped when first read, not at open; a domain without `invalidRecords: 'backup-and-skip'` keeps failing loud at open.
The lazy path needs the backend's synchronous per-record reads; another backend keeps the upstream loadAll path unchanged.
An empty per-record tree still calls loadAll once, because that call is the backend's legacy whole-unit bootstrap.

A rejected one-publish batch leaves memory and medium untouched; on a backend without that publish, a mid-batch failure leaves the earlier records durable and rejects with `batch-partial`, naming how many landed.

verification.testName: opens from document keys and reads no record
bounds the cache and re-reads an evicted record
serves keys, entries, and size exactly as the eager path does
writes through: a put is durable and visible without a re-read, deletes and updates follow
backs up and skips a record whose document fails its schema, on first read
keeps the open-time loud failure for an authoritative per-record domain
migrates a legacy whole-unit document into per-record documents, then hydrates lazily
commits a batch as ONE durable write and announces each key once
writes and announces nothing for an empty batch
applies duplicate keys in order, the last value winning, with one event per key
keeps memory and medium untouched when the one-publish batch is rejected
falls back to per-record writes and names exactly what landed when one fails mid-batch
serves a batch written through a lazy per-record table from its cache, with one durable write

verification.reason: Host-only storage infrastructure: no browser scenario reaches a domain table or its write chain directly.

telemetry.reason: In-process storage reads and schema validation inside the opening consumer's existing span; no fetch, socket, or long job of its own.
